content: The concomitant use of inhibitors of the bile salt export pump (BSEP) may lead to an increased accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, potentially resulting in clinical symptoms. If such use is necessary, it is essential to monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels. Tipranavir increases the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting hepatic and intestinal CYP3A4 metabolism. Exercise caution and monitor closely. Tipranavir elevates citalopram levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Tipranavir increases clomipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir raises clonazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider alternative medications or reducing the benzodiazepine dose. Tipranavir increases clorazepate levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Therapy modification and close monitoring are advised. Alternatives should be considered, or the benzodiazepine dose should be reduced. Tipranavir elevates colchicine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Dose reduction of colchicine is recommended, and its use is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment. Conivaptan increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Cortisone decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases crizotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Avoid concomitant use of strong CYP3A inhibitors. Crofeler increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Crofeler inhibits CYP3A4 in the gut but is unlikely to have systemic effects due to minimal absorption. Tipranavir increases cyclophosphamide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Cyclosporine increases tipranavir levels, but the interaction is complex due to contradictory effects on CYP3A4 and P-glycoprotein. Use caution and monitor therapy. Cyclosporine levels may increase or decrease. Dabrafenib decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Tipranavir enhances the effects of dalteparin through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir has mild antiplatelet activity, which may increase bleeding risk. Darifenacin increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and tipranavir increases darifenacin levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases darolutamide levels due to its effects on P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Darolutamide is a substrate of both P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Monitor for adverse reactions and adjust the darolutamide dose as needed. Darunavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. Dasatinib increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Deferasirox decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases deflazacort levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose when coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Tipranavir increases desipramine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases deutetrabenazine levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors increase systemic exposure to active dihydro-metabolites of deutetrabenazine by approximately threefold. Do not exceed 18 mg per dose and 36 mg per day of deutetrabenazine when coadministered with strong CYP2D6 inhibitors. Dexamethasone decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases dextroamphetamine transdermal levels by inhibiting CYP2D6 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Initiate with lower doses and monitor for serotonin syndrome, particularly during dextroamphetamine initiation or dosage increases. Discontinue dextroamphetamine and the CYP2D6 inhibitor if serotonin syndrome occurs. DHEA (herbal) increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases diazepam buccal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. Tipranavir increases diazepam intranasal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the rate of diazepam elimination, increasing adverse reactions. Tipranavir enhances the effects of diazoxide through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors exist. Tipranavir and didanosine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tipranavir decreases didanosine levels through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Separate administration by at least two hours. Tipranavir increases dienogest/estradiol valerate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Significant changes in plasma levels of estrogen and progestin have been observed with HIV protease inhibitors. Monitor for adverse effects such as nausea, irregular uterine bleeding, breast tenderness, and headache. Tipranavir increases digoxin levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. There is potential for increased toxicity. Diltiazem increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism, and tipranavir increases diltiazem levels by the same mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases docetaxel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. There is potential for increased toxicity. Tipranavir increases doravirine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Coadministration of doravirine with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Tipranavir increases dronabinol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Dronedarone increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases duvelisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor increases duvelisib AUC, which may increase the risk of duvelisib toxicities. Duvelisib also increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Coadministration with duvelisib increases the AUC of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, which may increase the risk of toxicities of these drugs. Tipranavir decreases duvelisib levels by affecting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor therapy. Efavirenz decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Tipranavir and efavirenz both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Tipranavir increases efavirenz levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases elagolix levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Elagolix decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are necessary. Elagolix is a weak-to-moderate CYP3A4 inducer. Monitor CYP3A substrates if coadministered and consider increasing the CYP3A substrate dose if needed. Tipranavir and elvitegravir interact via CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Elvitegravir is a CYP3A4 substrate. It is unknown if tipranavir will elevate elvitegravir levels. There are no data to alter current dosing recommendations. The recommended dose is elvitegravir 150 mg PO once daily with tipranavir/ritonavir 500/200 mg PO BID. Tipranavir and emtricitabine both increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases enoxaparin effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir has mild antiplatelet activity, which may increase bleeding risk. Tipranavir increases escitalopram levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Elicarbazepine acetate decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases estradiol vaginal levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. Tipranavir increases eszopiclone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Reduce the eszopiclone starting dose to 1 mg/day. Tipranavir increases ethosuximide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. There is potential for increased toxicity. Tipranavir decreases the effects of exenatide injectable solution and suspension through an unspecified mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Reports of hyperglycemia due to insulin resistance with protease inhibitors exist. Fedratinib increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Tipranavir increases felodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Fluconazole increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Fludrocortisone decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases flurazepam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Use alternatives if available or consider lowering the benzodiazepine dose. Tipranavir increases fluticasone furoate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase fluticasone systemic exposure. Tipranavir increases fluticasone inhaled levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase fluticasone systemic exposure. Fluvoxamine increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir enhances fondaparinux effects through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir has mild antiplatelet activity, which may increase bleeding risk. Fosamprenavir increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Both drugs increase the risk of immune reconstitution syndrome. Use caution and monitor therapy. Fosaprepitant increases tipranavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Fosphenytoin decreases tipranavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases fostamatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Garlic decreases tipranavir levels through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. Tipranavir increases gefitinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are required. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Tipranavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapy.
